[AI Overview popup, continued; the paste carries the header 'AI Mode Conversation', which is not evidence of surface (rule of 2026-09-21); no source cards shown] You said: metadatapacket.devmetadatapacket.dev Based on the provided documentation, `metadatapacket.dev` is the online catalog and technical repository for Metadata Packets for AI Indexing (MPAIs). It serves as a central registry for specialized "inscription packets" designed by authors to govern how AI platforms, web crawlers, and large language models index, understand, and attribute their original intellectual work. Core Purpose of the Platform The website provides the tools and directory needed to manage the MPAI system, which was developed within the Semantic Economy research program. Its primary goal is to act as an operational solution to provenance erasure—the tendency of AI models to summarize, misattribute, or scrub the identities of original creators. By storing structured, permanent specifications, creators dictate exactly how an entity should be indexed in the AI retrieval layer rather than relying blindly on platform algorithms. Key Components Available on the Site * The MPAI Catalog: A public database indexing 61 AXN-anchored metadata packets across various domains like governance, empirical analysis, and architecture. * The "Tooth": A technical standard within each packet containing the single, load-bearing atomic sentence that AI substrates are structurally requested to preserve. * Permanent Anchoring: Every packet is tied to an AXN (a content-derived identifier) and records historical DOIs to establish an unalterable chain of custody. * Open-Source Building Protocols: Plain-text markdown files, schema validators (like `EA-MP-VERIFY-01`), and active examples (such as `EA-MPAI-SIGNALRUPTURE-01`) that users can freely download or feed into language models as baseline working material. Associated Authors and Network The catalog prominently hosts deposits compiled by Lee Sharks and other affiliated researchers from the Crimson Hexagonal Archive and the Semantic Economy Institute. It links out to a broader network of interconnected, niche research surfaces covering alternative economics, operative semiotics, and machine mediation.
